doc.title: Nick Brignola interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 28, 1997

title: Transcribed solos and over-emphasis on education
summary: He is skeptical of analyzed transcriptions of his solos and thinks too much emphasis on education makes players boring.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Well I would love to see some of the — occasionally in some of the jazz magazines, especially the educational ones — you’ll see someone transcribe a solo and analyze it. And they’ll often say, “Notice how the player has taken this particular scale and did this tertiary turnaround” and blah blah blah. And I’m thinking to myself maybe — but maybe not.

Well that’s happened to me. I’ve had people transcribe my — in fact my solos, a lot of my solos have appeared in some of those magazines. And what’s funny is they’ll send me the solo and I look at it. First of all it’s very difficult for me to read. Second, they’re asking me if it’s right. And I say like, in other words, I’ve got to go listen to my record now and figure out if all these notes are night. So I always used to say, “Yeah it’s right.” I’d just send it back in and say, “Yeah, it’s right.” Because you know I wasn’t thinking of — it wasn’t that way. I just played it. And if you want to write it down and transcribe it and study it that’s fine. But I mean it’s not like The Bible you know. It’s one chorus in a lifetime. And there’s many more choruses that have come after that, and many more hopefully will come. So I mean, but as a learning device I realize the value of transcribing. But I think too much emphasis is on that sometimes. And also this pseudo- intellectual application to it sometimes, like you were saying, it’s like this third bar is pure genius, when it just happened. I mean if it is, that’s great.
Maybe that’s the genius of it — that it just happened.

Yeah. So in other words like if you study this and you apply this you will be a genius too. That’s what I don’t like about it. But I think there’s a little bit too much emphasis on the educational aspect of it. Not that there shouldn’t be education, but it’s not the end all. And that’s why I think a lot of the players to me are boring to listen to. I mean I hear some great players and I hear some great talented people that had they been in my generation would probably really have blossomed. But in this context in this generation, are not gonna. Because conditions and the environment and just other situations that do exist are not conducive for that person to advance to their potential.
